front.title: Algorithms for Cryptographic Message Syntax (CMS) Protection of Symmetric Key Package Content Types

abstract.t: This document describes the conventions for using several cryptographic algorithms with the Cryptographic Message Syntax (CMS) to protect the symmetric key package content type. Specifically, it includes conventions necessary to implement SignedData, EnvelopedData, EncryptedData, and AuthEnvelopedData.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: This document describes the conventions for using several cryptographic algorithms with the Cryptographic Message Syntax (CMS) to protect the symmetric key package content type defined in . Specifically, it includes conventions necessary to implement the following CMS content types: SignedData , EnvelopedData , EncryptedData , and AuthEnvelopedData . Familiarity with , , , and is assumed.
This document does not define any new algorithms; instead, it refers to previously defined algorithms.

section.name: Terminology
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in .

section.name: SignedData
section.t: If an implementation supports SignedData, then it MUST support the signature scheme RSA and SHOULD support the signature schemes RSA Probabilistic Signature Scheme (RSASSA-PSS) and Digital Signature Algorithm (DSA) . Additionally, implementations MUST support the hash function SHA-256 in concert with these signature schemes, and they SHOULD support the hash function SHA-1 . If an implementation supports SignedData, then it MAY support Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA) .

section.name: EnvelopedData
section.t: If an implementation supports EnvelopedData, then it MUST implement key transport, and it MAY implement key agreement.
When key transport is used, RSA encryption MUST be supported, and RSA Encryption Scheme - Optimal Asymmetric Encryption Padding (RSAES-OAEP) SHOULD be supported.
When key agreement is used, Diffie-Hellman (DH) ephemeral-static MUST be supported. When key agreement is used, Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH) MAY be supported.

Regardless of the key management technique choice, implementations MUST support AES-128 Key Wrap with Padding as the content-encryption algorithm. Implementations SHOULD support AES-256 Key Wrap with Padding as the content-encryption algorithm.

When key agreement is used, the same key-wrap algorithm MUST be used for both key and content encryption. If the content-encryption algorithm is AES-128 Key Wrap with Padding, then the key-wrap algorithm MUST be AES-128 Key Wrap with Padding . If the content-encryption algorithm is AES-256 Key Wrap with Padding, then the key-wrap algorithm MUST be AES-256 Key Wrap with Padding .

section.name: EncryptedData
section.t: If an implementation supports EncryptedData, then it MUST implement AES-128 Key Wrap with Padding and SHOULD implement AES-256 Key Wrap with Padding .

section.name: AuthEnvelopedData
section.t: If an implementation supports AuthEnvelopedData, then it MUST implement the EnvelopedData recommendations except for the content-encryption algorithm, which, in this case, MUST be AES-GCM ; the 128-bit version MUST be implemented, and the 256-bit version SHOULD be implemented. Implementations MAY also support AES-CCM .

section.name: Public Key Sizes
section.t: The easiest way to implement SignedData, EnvelopedData, and AuthEnvelopedData is with public key certificates . If an implementation supports RSA, RSASSA-PSS, DSA, RSAES-OAEP, or Diffie-Hellman, then it MUST support key lengths from 1024-bit to 2048-bit, inclusive. If an implementation supports ECDSA or ECDH, then it MUST support keys on P-256.
